group.passage:
Roller skating is now a common way to have fun and stay fit, but its story began with a painful mistake. In the 1700s, a Belgian inventor named John Joseph Merlin lived in London, where he made clever machines and musical instruments. One of his ideas was to put small metal wheels under a pair of boots. With them, people could move across a floor as if they were skating on ice. Merlin was very [[1]] of this invention and wanted to show it to as many people as possible.
His chance came when he was invited to a fancy party. Instead of walking through the door like every other [[2]], he rolled into the hall while playing the violin. At first, everyone stared at him in wonder. Sadly, his boots had no brakes, so he had no way to [[3]] once he picked up speed. Unable to turn, he shot across the room and [[4]] into a huge mirror. The mirror broke into pieces, his violin was ruined, and Merlin himself was badly [[5]].
After that night, many people thought roller skates were [[6]] to anyone who wore them. For years afterward, few people wanted to try them. The main problem was that the wheels were set in a single [[7]], which made the skates hard to control.
In 1863, an American named James Plimpton finally solved this problem. He placed four wheels in two pairs, one pair under the toes and one under the heel. A skater could now turn simply by moving his or her [[8]] to one side, which made skating much safer. As a result, skating soon became [[9]] in America and Europe, where thousands of people bought skates. Today, Merlin's crash is often [[10]] as the funny start of a sport loved around the world.

1.explanation_zh: be proud of（以……為傲、對……很得意）是固定搭配。Merlin 對自己的發明很得意，所以後半句說他想讓越多人看到越好（wanted to show it to as many people as possible）。
evidence: Merlin was very [[1]] of this invention and wanted to show it to as many people as possible.

option_notes_zh.A: popular（受歡迎的）要說「受某人歡迎」用 popular with，was very popular of 不合搭配；而且這句說的是 Merlin 自己對發明的感受。
option_notes_zh.B: hurt 當形容詞是「受傷的、難過的」，不和 of 搭配；而且他想把發明展示給大家看，心情是得意，不是難過。
option_notes_zh.C: guest（名詞，客人）詞性不合：空格在 was very 之後、介系詞 of 之前，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.D: described（動詞 describe 的過去式或過去分詞，描述）詞性不合：空格在 was very 之後、介系詞 of 之前，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.E: row（名詞，一排、一列）詞性不合：空格在 was very 之後、介系詞 of 之前，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.G: slow down（片語動詞，減速、慢下來）詞性不合：空格在 was very 之後、介系詞 of 之前，需要形容詞。
option_notes_zh.H: was very dangerous of 不合搭配；dangerous（危險的）用來形容事物或處境，不能表示 Merlin 對發明的感受。
option_notes_zh.I: smashed 是 smash 的過去式或過去分詞（撞碎），was very smashed of 不合文法，意思也不通。
option_notes_zh.J: weight（名詞，重量、重心）詞性不合：空格在 was very 之後、介系詞 of 之前，需要形容詞。

1.strategy_zh: 看到 be very ___ of，先想哪個形容詞常接 of；後半句「想讓越多人看到越好」說明他很得意。
hints: 空格在 was very 之後、of 之前，需要形容詞。
哪個形容詞常和 of 連用，表示對某事的感受？
他想把發明展示給越多人看越好，心情是……

2.explanation_zh: every other＋單數名詞表示「其他每一個……」。前一句說他受邀參加一場盛大的派對（invited to a fancy party）；其他賓客都從門口走進來，他卻溜著輪子進場，所以空格是「客人」。
evidence: Instead of walking through the door like every other [[2]], he rolled into the hall while playing the violin.
His chance came when he was invited to a fancy party.

option_notes_zh.A: popular（形容詞，受歡迎的）詞性不合：空格在 every other 之後，需要單數可數名詞。
option_notes_zh.B: hurt 是動詞（傷害）或形容詞（受傷的）；當名詞是「傷痛」，like every other hurt 不通，這裡需要指人的可數名詞。
option_notes_zh.D: described（動詞 describe 的過去式或過去分詞，描述）詞性不合：空格在 every other 之後，需要單數可數名詞。
option_notes_zh.E: every other row（其他每一排）不通；這裡拿來比較的是走進派對大廳的人。
option_notes_zh.F: proud（形容詞，得意的、驕傲的）詞性不合：空格在 every other 之後，需要單數可數名詞。
option_notes_zh.G: slow down（片語動詞，減速、慢下來）詞性不合：空格在 every other 之後，需要單數可數名詞。
option_notes_zh.H: dangerous（形容詞，危險的）詞性不合：空格在 every other 之後，需要單數可數名詞。
option_notes_zh.I: smashed（動詞 smash 的過去式或過去分詞，猛撞、撞碎）詞性不合：空格在 every other 之後，需要單數可數名詞。
option_notes_zh.J: every other weight（其他每個重量）不通；會從門口走進派對的是人。

2.strategy_zh: every other 後面接單數名詞；派對上「從門口走進來」的是誰？
hints: every other 後面需要單數名詞。
前一句說他受邀參加什麼？
派對上和他一樣受邀的人叫什麼？

3.explanation_zh: had no way to＋原形動詞（沒辦法做某事）。前半句說他的靴子沒有煞車（had no brakes），so 帶出結果：一旦速度變快（once he picked up speed），他就沒辦法「減速」。
evidence: Sadly, his boots had no brakes, so he had no way to [[3]] once he picked up speed.

option_notes_zh.A: popular（形容詞，受歡迎的）詞性不合：空格在 had no way to 之後，需要原形動詞。
option_notes_zh.B: hurt 是及物動詞，要接受詞（hurt someone）；had no way to hurt 後面沒有受詞，而且「沒辦法傷害」和沒有煞車的因果不合。
option_notes_zh.C: guest（名詞，客人）詞性不合：空格在 had no way to 之後，需要原形動詞。
option_notes_zh.D: described 是過去式或過去分詞，不能放在 to 後面；describe 也要接受詞。
option_notes_zh.E: row 當動詞是「划（船）」，no way to row 和溜冰、煞車無關；沒有煞車造成的問題是速度降不下來。
option_notes_zh.F: proud（形容詞，得意的、驕傲的）詞性不合：空格在 had no way to 之後，需要原形動詞。
option_notes_zh.H: dangerous（形容詞，危險的）詞性不合：空格在 had no way to 之後，需要原形動詞。
option_notes_zh.I: smashed 是過去式或過去分詞，不能放在 to 後面。
option_notes_zh.J: weight（名詞，重量、重心）詞性不合：空格在 had no way to 之後，需要原形動詞。

3.strategy_zh: so 前面說「沒有煞車」，後面就是結果：速度一快就……
hints: had no way to 後面要原形動詞。
煞車（brakes）的功用是什麼？
速度變快以後，他最需要做到的是……

4.explanation_zh: and 連接兩個過去式動詞：shot across the room and ___ into a huge mirror。他不會轉彎，衝過整個房間「撞上」一面大鏡子；下一句說鏡子碎成片（The mirror broke into pieces）。
evidence: Unable to turn, he shot across the room and [[4]] into a huge mirror.
The mirror broke into pieces, his violin was ruined, and Merlin himself was badly [[5]].

option_notes_zh.A: popular（形容詞，受歡迎的）詞性不合：空格和 shot 由 and 連接，是主詞 he 的過去式動詞，後接 into a huge mirror。
option_notes_zh.B: hurt 的過去式也是 hurt，但 hurt 要接受詞，hurt into a huge mirror 不通。
option_notes_zh.C: guest（名詞，客人）詞性不合：空格和 shot 由 and 連接，是主詞 he 的過去式動詞，後接 into a huge mirror。
option_notes_zh.D: described into a huge mirror 不通；describe（描述）要接受詞，也和衝過房間的動作無關。
option_notes_zh.E: row 當動詞是「划船」，而且是原形，和 shot 的過去式不一致；row into a mirror 也不通。
option_notes_zh.F: proud（形容詞，得意的、驕傲的）詞性不合：空格和 shot 由 and 連接，是主詞 he 的過去式動詞，後接 into a huge mirror。
option_notes_zh.G: slow down 是原形，和 shot 的過去式不一致；而且他正是因為停不下來才撞上鏡子。
option_notes_zh.H: dangerous（形容詞，危險的）詞性不合：空格和 shot 由 and 連接，是主詞 he 的過去式動詞，後接 into a huge mirror。
option_notes_zh.J: weight（名詞，重量、重心）詞性不合：空格和 shot 由 and 連接，是主詞 he 的過去式動詞，後接 into a huge mirror。

4.strategy_zh: and 前後的動詞時態一致；下一句「鏡子碎成片」說明他撞上了鏡子。
hints: 空格和 shot 由 and 連接，要過去式動詞。
他不會轉彎又衝得很快，結果會怎樣？
下一句說鏡子怎麼了？

5.explanation_zh: badly hurt（傷得很重）是常見說法；was＋過去分詞表示被動。他撞碎鏡子、小提琴也毀了，他本人也「受了重傷」；第一段說這是 a painful mistake（痛苦的錯誤），也是呼應。
evidence: The mirror broke into pieces, his violin was ruined, and Merlin himself was badly [[5]].
Roller skating is now a common way to have fun and stay fit, but its story began with a painful mistake.

option_notes_zh.A: was badly popular 不通：badly（嚴重地）修飾的是受傷這類狀態；撞上鏡子也不會讓他變得受歡迎。
option_notes_zh.C: guest（名詞，客人）詞性不合：空格在 was badly 之後，需要過去分詞（被動）。
option_notes_zh.D: was badly described（被描述得很糟）不通；這裡說的是他撞上鏡子後身體的情況。
option_notes_zh.E: row 是名詞（一排）或原形動詞（划船），was badly row 不合文法。
option_notes_zh.F: was badly proud 不通；撞碎鏡子、毀了小提琴，談不上得意。
option_notes_zh.G: slow down 是原形片語動詞，was badly slow down 不合文法。
option_notes_zh.H: was badly dangerous 不通；這裡說的是撞擊後 Merlin 本人的狀況，不是說他很危險。
option_notes_zh.I: smashed 用在東西被砸碎；Merlin himself was badly smashed 用來說人不通，被撞碎的是鏡子。
option_notes_zh.J: weight（名詞，重量、重心）詞性不合：空格在 was badly 之後，需要過去分詞（被動）。

5.strategy_zh: badly 修飾什麼？撞上一面大鏡子以後，人會怎樣？
hints: was badly 後面需要過去分詞。
撞上一面大鏡子，人通常會……
第一段說這是一個「痛苦的」錯誤。

6.explanation_zh: be dangerous to＋人（對某人有危險）；空格在 were 之後，需要形容詞當補語。After that night 指 Merlin 撞上鏡子、受重傷的那一晚；下一句說之後許多年很少人想試（few people wanted to try them），所以大家認為溜冰鞋對穿上它的人很「危險」。
evidence: After that night, many people thought roller skates were [[6]] to anyone who wore them.
For years afterward, few people wanted to try them.

option_notes_zh.A: popular（受歡迎的）不和 to anyone 搭配（受某人歡迎要說 popular with）；而且下一句說之後許多年 few people wanted to try them（很少人想試），可見溜冰鞋並不受歡迎。popular 要用在第 9 格（Plimpton 改良之後）。
option_notes_zh.B: hurt 當形容詞是「受傷的」，roller skates were hurt to anyone 不通；會受傷的是人，不是溜冰鞋。
option_notes_zh.C: guest（名詞，客人）詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、to anyone 之前，需要形容詞當補語。
option_notes_zh.D: were described to anyone who wore them（被描述給穿的人聽）不通；這句說的是人們對溜冰鞋的看法：穿上它會受傷。
option_notes_zh.E: row（名詞，一排、一列）詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、to anyone 之前，需要形容詞當補語。
option_notes_zh.F: proud 形容人的感受，roller skates were proud 不通；proud to 後面接動詞（proud to say），不接人。
option_notes_zh.G: slow down（片語動詞，減速、慢下來）詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、to anyone 之前，需要形容詞當補語。
option_notes_zh.I: smashed 當形容詞是「被砸壞的」，were smashed to anyone 不通；下一句說大家不想試，原因是會讓人受傷，不是溜冰鞋壞了。
option_notes_zh.J: weight（名詞，重量、重心）詞性不合：空格在 were 之後、to anyone 之前，需要形容詞當補語。

6.strategy_zh: 先看下一句：之後許多年很少人想試。那一晚發生了什麼事，讓大家覺得溜冰鞋對穿的人不安全？
hints: were ___ to anyone：空格需要形容詞當補語。
After that night 指的是哪一晚？發生了什麼事？
下一句說之後很少人想試穿溜冰鞋。

7.explanation_zh: in a single row（排成一直排）。輪子全排在同一直線上，所以溜冰鞋很難控制；第四段 Plimpton 把四個輪子分成前後兩對（in two pairs），才解決了這個問題。
evidence: The main problem was that the wheels were set in a single [[7]], which made the skates hard to control.
He placed four wheels in two pairs, one pair under the toes and one under the heel.

option_notes_zh.A: popular（形容詞，受歡迎的）詞性不合：空格在 a single 之後，需要單數名詞。
option_notes_zh.B: hurt 當名詞是「傷痛」，the wheels were set in a single hurt 不通。
option_notes_zh.C: the wheels were set in a single guest 不通。
option_notes_zh.D: described（動詞 describe 的過去式或過去分詞，描述）詞性不合：空格在 a single 之後，需要單數名詞。
option_notes_zh.F: proud（形容詞，得意的、驕傲的）詞性不合：空格在 a single 之後，需要單數名詞。
option_notes_zh.G: slow down（片語動詞，減速、慢下來）詞性不合：空格在 a single 之後，需要單數名詞。
option_notes_zh.H: dangerous（形容詞，危險的）詞性不合：空格在 a single 之後，需要單數名詞。
option_notes_zh.I: smashed（動詞 smash 的過去式或過去分詞，猛撞、撞碎）詞性不合：空格在 a single 之後，需要單數名詞。
option_notes_zh.J: set in a single weight（排成一個重量）不通；這裡說的是輪子排列的方式。

7.strategy_zh: 這句說輪子「怎麼排」；對照第四段 in two pairs 的改良。
hints: a single 後面需要單數名詞。
這句在說輪子的排列方式。
第四段說改良後的輪子分成兩對。

8.explanation_zh: move one’s weight to one side（把重心移到一邊）。Plimpton 的溜冰鞋前後各有一對輪子，溜冰的人只要把「重心」往一側移就能轉彎，所以安全多了。
evidence: A skater could now turn simply by moving his or her [[8]] to one side, which made skating much safer.

option_notes_zh.A: popular（形容詞，受歡迎的）詞性不合：空格在 his or her 之後，需要名詞。
option_notes_zh.B: hurt 當名詞是「傷痛」，moving his or her hurt to one side 不通。
option_notes_zh.C: moving his or her guest to one side（把客人移到一邊）不通；這裡說的是溜冰的人怎麼轉彎。
option_notes_zh.D: described（動詞 describe 的過去式或過去分詞，描述）詞性不合：空格在 his or her 之後，需要名詞。
option_notes_zh.E: moving his or her row to one side 不通；row 是「一排」，溜冰的人轉彎時移動的是身體的重心。
option_notes_zh.F: proud（形容詞，得意的、驕傲的）詞性不合：空格在 his or her 之後，需要名詞。
option_notes_zh.G: slow down（片語動詞，減速、慢下來）詞性不合：空格在 his or her 之後，需要名詞。
option_notes_zh.H: dangerous（形容詞，危險的）詞性不合：空格在 his or her 之後，需要名詞。
option_notes_zh.I: smashed（動詞 smash 的過去式或過去分詞，猛撞、撞碎）詞性不合：空格在 his or her 之後，需要名詞。

8.strategy_zh: 溜冰時想轉彎，要把身體的什麼移到一邊？
hints: his or her 後面需要名詞。
溜冰的人靠什麼方法轉彎？
把身體的「重心」往左或往右移。

9.explanation_zh: became＋形容詞（變得……）。As a result（結果）承接前一句：轉彎變容易，溜冰安全多了（much safer）；所以溜冰很快在美國和歐洲變得「受歡迎」，成千上萬的人買了溜冰鞋。最後一句也說這是一項風靡全世界的運動（a sport loved around the world）。
evidence: As a result, skating soon became [[9]] in America and Europe, where thousands of people bought skates.
A skater could now turn simply by moving his or her [[8]] to one side, which made skating much safer.

option_notes_zh.B: hurt 當形容詞是「受傷的」，用來形容人；skating became hurt 不通，主詞是 skating（溜冰這項活動）。
option_notes_zh.C: guest（名詞，客人）詞性不合：空格在 became 之後，需要形容詞當補語。
option_notes_zh.D: described 是過去分詞，skating became described 不通。
option_notes_zh.E: row（名詞，一排、一列）詞性不合：空格在 became 之後，需要形容詞當補語。
option_notes_zh.F: skating soon became proud 不通；proud 形容人的感受，主詞是 skating（溜冰這項活動）。
option_notes_zh.G: slow down（片語動詞，減速、慢下來）詞性不合：空格在 became 之後，需要形容詞當補語。
option_notes_zh.H: skating soon became dangerous（溜冰變得很危險）只看本句說得通，但 As a result 承接前一句的 which made skating much safer（溜冰安全多了），結果不會是變得危險；dangerous 要用在第 6 格（Merlin 受傷之後）。
option_notes_zh.I: smashed 當形容詞是「被砸壞的」，skating became smashed 不通。
option_notes_zh.J: weight（名詞，重量、重心）詞性不合：空格在 became 之後，需要形容詞當補語。

9.strategy_zh: As a result 表示結果：前一句說溜冰安全多了，本句後半又說成千上萬的人買了溜冰鞋。這樣的活動會變得怎麼樣？
hints: became 後面需要形容詞。
As a result 承接前一句的哪個改變？
很多人搶著買、搶著玩，表示這項活動很……

10.explanation_zh: be described as（被形容成……、被說成……）是固定搭配。Merlin 撞上鏡子那件事，現在常「被說成」是這項風靡全世界的運動有趣的開端。
evidence: Today, Merlin's crash is often [[10]] as the funny start of a sport loved around the world.

option_notes_zh.A: is often popular as the funny start 不通：說一件過去的意外「常常很受歡迎」不合理；as 前面要能表示「被看作、被說成」。
option_notes_zh.B: is often hurt as 不通；hurt 不接 as，而且主詞是 Merlin’s crash（那次撞擊），不是人。
option_notes_zh.C: guest（名詞，客人）詞性不合：空格在 is often 之後，需要過去分詞（被動）。
option_notes_zh.E: row 是名詞或原形動詞，is often row as 不合文法。
option_notes_zh.F: is often proud as 不通；proud 形容人，主詞是那次撞擊。
option_notes_zh.G: slow down 是原形，is often slow down 不合文法。
option_notes_zh.H: is often dangerous as 不通；那次撞擊已經過去，說它「常常很危險」不合理。
option_notes_zh.I: is often smashed as 不通；主詞是那次撞擊事件，不能被砸碎。
option_notes_zh.J: weight（名詞，重量、重心）詞性不合：空格在 is often 之後，需要過去分詞（被動）。

10.strategy_zh: 看到 as，想到 be described as（被形容為）；主詞是那次撞擊事件。
hints: is often 後面需要過去分詞。
哪個動詞常和 as 連用，表示「被說成……」？
那次意外現在被人們怎麼看待？

translation_zh.text:
溜冰現在是常見的娛樂和健身方式，但它的故事是從一個痛苦的錯誤開始的。1700 年代，一位名叫約翰‧約瑟夫‧梅林的比利時發明家住在倫敦，製作巧妙的機器和樂器。他的點子之一，是在一雙靴子底下裝上小小的金屬輪子。穿上它，人們就能像在冰上溜冰一樣在地板上移動。梅林對這項發明非常得意，想讓越多人看到越好。
他的機會在受邀參加一場盛大派對時來了。他不像其他客人那樣從門口走進去，而是一邊拉小提琴，一邊溜進大廳。起初大家都驚奇地盯著他看。可惜他的靴子沒有煞車，一旦速度變快，他就沒辦法減速。他也不會轉彎，結果衝過整個房間，撞上一面巨大的鏡子。鏡子碎成片，小提琴毀了，梅林自己也受了重傷。
那一晚之後，很多人認為溜冰鞋對穿上它的人很危險。之後許多年，很少人想要嘗試。主要的問題在於輪子排成一直排，讓溜冰鞋很難控制。
1863 年，一位名叫詹姆斯‧普林普頓的美國人終於解決了這個問題。他把四個輪子分成兩對，一對在腳尖下，一對在腳跟下。溜冰的人現在只要把重心移到一邊就能轉彎，溜冰因此安全多了。結果，溜冰很快就在美國和歐洲受到歡迎，成千上萬的人在那裡買了溜冰鞋。如今，梅林那次撞擊常被說成是這項風靡全世界的運動有趣的開端。

evidence: Merlin was very [[1]] of this invention and wanted to show it to as many people as possible.
1.explanation_zh: be proud of 為固定搭配，且他想向眾人展示，表示對發明感到驕傲。

evidence: His chance came when he was invited to a fancy party.
Instead of walking through the door like every other [[2]], he rolled into the hall while playing the violin.
2.explanation_zh: 受邀參加派對，其他人是賓客；every other 後接單數名詞 guest。

evidence: Sadly, his boots had no brakes, so he had no way to [[3]] once he picked up speed.
3.explanation_zh: 沒有煞車，所以速度起來後無法減速；to 後接原形動詞片語 slow down。

evidence: Unable to turn, he shot across the room and [[4]] into a huge mirror.
The mirror broke into pieces, his violin was ruined, and Merlin himself was badly [[5]].
4.explanation_zh: 與 shot 並列的過去式動詞，撞進鏡子使其碎裂，smashed into 最合。

evidence: The mirror broke into pieces, his violin was ruined, and Merlin himself was badly [[5]].
5.explanation_zh: 撞碎鏡子後本人受重傷，be badly hurt 為常見搭配。

evidence: After that night, many people thought roller skates were [[6]] to anyone who wore them.
For years afterward, few people wanted to try them.
6.explanation_zh: 發生意外後人們認為溜冰鞋對穿的人很危險，因此很少人想嘗試。

evidence: The main problem was that the wheels were set in a single [[7]], which made the skates hard to control.
He placed four wheels in two pairs, one pair under the toes and one under the heel.
7.explanation_zh: 輪子排成單一一排而難以控制，後來改為兩對；in a single row。

evidence: A skater could now turn simply by moving his or her [[8]] to one side, which made skating much safer.
8.explanation_zh: 溜冰者把重心（體重）移向一側即可轉彎，his or her 後接名詞 weight。

evidence: As a result, skating soon became [[9]] in America and Europe, where thousands of people bought skates.
9.explanation_zh: 數千人購買溜冰鞋，表示溜冰變得流行。

evidence: Today, Merlin's crash is often [[10]] as the funny start of a sport loved around the world.
10.explanation_zh: be described as 為固定用法，意為「被描述為」。

evidence: Merlin was very [[1]] of this invention and wanted to show it to as many people as possible.
1.explanation_zh: be proud of 是固定搭配，且他想把發明展示給更多人，表示以此為傲。

evidence: Instead of walking through the door like every other [[2]], he rolled into the hall while playing the violin.
2.explanation_zh: 他受邀參加派對，空格是 every other 後的可數名詞，指其他受邀的客人。

evidence: Sadly, his boots had no brakes, so he had no way to [[3]] once he picked up speed.
3.explanation_zh: 靴子沒有煞車，加速後無法減速；to 後接原形動詞片語 slow down。

evidence: Unable to turn, he shot across the room and [[4]] into a huge mirror.
4.explanation_zh: 與 shot 並列的過去式動詞，撞進大鏡子並使其碎裂，用 smashed。

evidence: The mirror broke into pieces, his violin was ruined, and Merlin himself was badly [[5]].
5.explanation_zh: 鏡子碎了、小提琴毀了，他自己也 badly hurt（受重傷）。

evidence: After that night, many people thought roller skates were [[6]] to anyone who wore them.
6.explanation_zh: 事故後人們認為溜冰鞋對穿的人有危險，後文也說很少人想嘗試。

evidence: The main problem was that the wheels were set in a single [[7]], which made the skates hard to control.
7.explanation_zh: 輪子排成單一一列（in a single row）難以控制；後文改成兩對輪子。

evidence: A skater could now turn simply by moving his or her [[8]] to one side, which made skating much safer.
8.explanation_zh: 滑冰者把身體重心（weight）移向一側即可轉彎。

evidence: As a result, skating soon became [[9]] in America and Europe, where thousands of people bought skates.
9.explanation_zh: 數千人購買溜冰鞋，表示溜冰變得很受歡迎。

evidence: Today, Merlin's crash is often [[10]] as the funny start of a sport loved around the world.
10.explanation_zh: be described as ... 被描述為有趣的開端，被動語態用過去分詞。

A.evidence: Merlin was very [[1]] of this invention and wanted to show it to as many people as possible.
A.explanation_zh: popular 的對象用 with／among，沒有 be popular of 的用法；「他很受這項發明歡迎」也說不通。

B.evidence: Merlin was very [[1]] of this invention and wanted to show it to as many people as possible.
B.explanation_zh: hurt 當形容詞是「受傷的、難過的」，不接 of 表示對象；「對發明感到受傷」也與後面「想讓越多人看越好」矛盾。

C.evidence: Merlin was very [[1]] of this invention and wanted to show it to as many people as possible.
C.explanation_zh: very 後面要接形容詞（be very ___ of），guest 是名詞。

D.evidence: Merlin was very [[1]] of this invention and wanted to show it to as many people as possible.
D.explanation_zh: was very described of 不合語法；describe 的被動不接 of，very 也不直接修飾它。

E.evidence: Merlin was very [[1]] of this invention and wanted to show it to as many people as possible.
E.explanation_zh: row 是名詞／動詞，不能放在 was very 後面再接 of。

G.evidence: Merlin was very [[1]] of this invention and wanted to show it to as many people as possible.
G.explanation_zh: slow down 是動詞片語，不能放在 was very 後面當補語。

H.evidence: Merlin was very [[1]] of this invention and wanted to show it to as many people as possible.
H.explanation_zh: dangerous 不接 of 表示對象；他想把發明展示給越多人看越好，表示的是得意（proud of）。

I.evidence: Merlin was very [[1]] of this invention and wanted to show it to as many people as possible.
I.explanation_zh: was very smashed of 不合語法，語意也不通。

J.evidence: Merlin was very [[1]] of this invention and wanted to show it to as many people as possible.
J.explanation_zh: weight 是名詞，不能放在 very 後面接 of。

A.evidence: Instead of walking through the door like every other [[2]], he rolled into the hall while playing the violin.
A.explanation_zh: every other 後面要接單數名詞，popular 是形容詞。

B.evidence: Instead of walking through the door like every other [[2]], he rolled into the hall while playing the violin.
B.explanation_zh: hurt 當名詞是「傷痛」，「像其他每一個傷痛一樣從門口走進來」說不通；走進派對的是受邀的客人。

D.evidence: Instead of walking through the door like every other [[2]], he rolled into the hall while playing the violin.
D.explanation_zh: described 是過去分詞，不能當 every other 後面的名詞。

E.evidence: Instead of walking through the door like every other [[2]], he rolled into the hall while playing the violin.
E.explanation_zh: row 是「一排」，「像其他每一排一樣從門口走進來」說不通；從門口走進派對的是客人。

F.evidence: Instead of walking through the door like every other [[2]], he rolled into the hall while playing the violin.
F.explanation_zh: proud 是形容詞，every other 後面要接名詞。

G.evidence: Instead of walking through the door like every other [[2]], he rolled into the hall while playing the violin.
G.explanation_zh: slow down 是動詞片語，every other 後面要接名詞。

H.evidence: Instead of walking through the door like every other [[2]], he rolled into the hall while playing the violin.
H.explanation_zh: dangerous 是形容詞，every other 後面要接名詞。

I.evidence: Instead of walking through the door like every other [[2]], he rolled into the hall while playing the violin.
I.explanation_zh: smashed 是動詞過去式／過去分詞，every other 後面要接名詞。

J.evidence: Instead of walking through the door like every other [[2]], he rolled into the hall while playing the violin.
J.explanation_zh: 「像其他每一個重量一樣從門口走進來」說不通；走進派對的是人。

A.evidence: Sadly, his boots had no brakes, so he had no way to [[3]] once he picked up speed.
A.explanation_zh: to 後面要接原形動詞，popular 是形容詞。

B.evidence: Sadly, his boots had no brakes, so he had no way to [[3]] once he picked up speed.
B.explanation_zh: hurt 不及物時是「疼痛」，「速度起來後沒辦法疼痛」與「沒有煞車」的因果不合；沒有煞車造成的是無法減速。

C.evidence: Sadly, his boots had no brakes, so he had no way to [[3]] once he picked up speed.
C.explanation_zh: to 後面要接原形動詞，guest 是名詞。

D.evidence: Sadly, his boots had no brakes, so he had no way to [[3]] once he picked up speed.
D.explanation_zh: to 後面要接原形動詞，described 是過去分詞；describe 也必須有受詞。

E.evidence: Sadly, his boots had no brakes, so he had no way to [[3]] once he picked up speed.
E.explanation_zh: row 當動詞是「划船」，「沒辦法划船」與鞋子沒有煞車無關。

F.evidence: Sadly, his boots had no brakes, so he had no way to [[3]] once he picked up speed.
F.explanation_zh: to 後面要接原形動詞，proud 是形容詞。

H.evidence: Sadly, his boots had no brakes, so he had no way to [[3]] once he picked up speed.
H.explanation_zh: to 後面要接原形動詞，dangerous 是形容詞。

I.evidence: Sadly, his boots had no brakes, so he had no way to [[3]] once he picked up speed.
I.explanation_zh: to 後面要接原形動詞，smashed 是過去式；「沒辦法砸碎」也與沒有煞車的因果不合。

J.evidence: Sadly, his boots had no brakes, so he had no way to [[3]] once he picked up speed.
J.explanation_zh: weight 當動詞是「加重量於」，須接受詞；「沒辦法加重」與沒有煞車無關。

A.evidence: Unable to turn, he shot across the room and [[4]] into a huge mirror.
A.explanation_zh: 與過去式 shot 對等，要接過去式動詞，popular 是形容詞。

B.evidence: Unable to turn, he shot across the room and [[4]] into a huge mirror.
B.explanation_zh: hurt 是及物動詞「弄傷」，沒有「撞進去」的意思，he hurt into a huge mirror 不成句。

C.evidence: Unable to turn, he shot across the room and [[4]] into a huge mirror.
C.explanation_zh: 與過去式 shot 對等，要接過去式動詞，guest 是名詞。

D.evidence: Unable to turn, he shot across the room and [[4]] into a huge mirror.
D.explanation_zh: describe 須接受詞，也沒有「撞進」的意思，described into a huge mirror 說不通。

E.evidence: Unable to turn, he shot across the room and [[4]] into a huge mirror.
E.explanation_zh: 與過去式 shot 對等要用過去式，row 時態不合；在室內「划船進鏡子」也不合情境。

F.evidence: Unable to turn, he shot across the room and [[4]] into a huge mirror.
F.explanation_zh: 與過去式 shot 對等，要接過去式動詞，proud 是形容詞。

G.evidence: Sadly, his boots had no brakes
G.explanation_zh: 前文說鞋子沒有煞車、無法減速，不可能「減速撞進鏡子」；slow down 也不是與 shot 對等的過去式。

H.evidence: Unable to turn, he shot across the room and [[4]] into a huge mirror.
H.explanation_zh: 與過去式 shot 對等，要接過去式動詞，dangerous 是形容詞。

J.evidence: Unable to turn, he shot across the room and [[4]] into a huge mirror.
J.explanation_zh: weight 是名詞或「加重」的動詞，時態也不是過去式，weight into a huge mirror 說不通。

A.evidence: The mirror broke into pieces, his violin was ruined, and Merlin himself was badly [[5]].
A.explanation_zh: 這句列出事故的損害（鏡子碎、琴毀），「他本人嚴重地受歡迎」不合；badly 也不修飾 popular。

C.evidence: The mirror broke into pieces, his violin was ruined, and Merlin himself was badly [[5]].
C.explanation_zh: was badly 後面要接過去分詞或形容詞，guest 是名詞。

D.evidence: The mirror broke into pieces, his violin was ruined, and Merlin himself was badly [[5]].
D.explanation_zh: was badly described 是「被描述得很差」，與事故中鏡子碎掉、小提琴毀掉並列不合；這裡要說他本人受了傷。

E.evidence: The mirror broke into pieces, his violin was ruined, and Merlin himself was badly [[5]].
E.explanation_zh: was badly 後面要接過去分詞或形容詞，row 是名詞／原形動詞。

F.evidence: The mirror broke into pieces, his violin was ruined, and Merlin himself was badly [[5]].
F.explanation_zh: badly proud 不成搭配，「嚴重地自豪」也與事故的損害不合。

G.evidence: The mirror broke into pieces, his violin was ruined, and Merlin himself was badly [[5]].
G.explanation_zh: slow down 是原形動詞片語，不能放在 was badly 後面。

H.evidence: The mirror broke into pieces, his violin was ruined, and Merlin himself was badly [[5]].
H.explanation_zh: badly dangerous 不成搭配；這裡說的是他在事故中受到的結果，不是他很危險。

I.evidence: The mirror broke into pieces, his violin was ruined, and Merlin himself was badly [[5]].
I.explanation_zh: smash 是「把東西砸碎」，badly smashed 用於鏡子、車子等物品；人在事故中受傷要用 hurt／injured，人也不會像鏡子一樣碎掉。

J.evidence: The mirror broke into pieces, his violin was ruined, and Merlin himself was badly [[5]].
J.explanation_zh: was badly 後面要接過去分詞或形容詞，weight 是名詞。

A.evidence: For years afterward, few people wanted to try them.
A.explanation_zh: 下一句說多年來很少人想嘗試，溜冰鞋不可能被認為受歡迎；popular 的對象也用 with，不用 to。

B.evidence: After that night, many people thought roller skates were [[6]] to anyone who wore them.
B.explanation_zh: hurt 作形容詞指人「受傷的」，roller skates were hurt to anyone 不合語法也說不通。

C.evidence: After that night, many people thought roller skates were [[6]] to anyone who wore them.
C.explanation_zh: were 後面接單數可數名詞須有冠詞，「溜冰鞋是客人」也說不通；這裡要形容詞。

D.evidence: After that night, many people thought roller skates were [[6]] to anyone who wore them.
D.explanation_zh: were described to anyone who wore them「被描述給任何穿的人」說不通；撞鏡事故後人們的看法是溜冰鞋危險。

E.evidence: After that night, many people thought roller skates were [[6]] to anyone who wore them.
E.explanation_zh: 這裡要形容詞作補語，row 是名詞。

F.evidence: After that night, many people thought roller skates were [[6]] to anyone who wore them.
F.explanation_zh: 物品不會自豪，roller skates were proud to anyone 說不通。

G.evidence: After that night, many people thought roller skates were [[6]] to anyone who wore them.
G.explanation_zh: were 後面不能接原形動詞片語 slow down。

I.evidence: After that night, many people thought roller skates were [[6]] to anyone who wore them.
I.explanation_zh: were smashed to anyone who wore them 說不通；事故後人們認為溜冰鞋對穿的人很危險。

J.evidence: After that night, many people thought roller skates were [[6]] to anyone who wore them.
J.explanation_zh: 這裡要形容詞作補語，weight 是名詞。

A.evidence: The main problem was that the wheels were set in a single [[7]], which made the skates hard to control.
A.explanation_zh: a single 後面要接名詞，popular 是形容詞。

B.evidence: The main problem was that the wheels were set in a single [[7]], which made the skates hard to control.
B.explanation_zh: 「輪子裝在單一個傷痛裡」說不通；這裡說的是輪子的排列方式。

C.evidence: He placed four wheels in two pairs, one pair under the toes and one under the heel.
C.explanation_zh: 輪子不會裝在「一位客人」裡；後文以 four wheels in two pairs 對比，說的是輪子原本排成一排。

D.evidence: The main problem was that the wheels were set in a single [[7]], which made the skates hard to control.
D.explanation_zh: a single 後面要接名詞，described 是過去分詞。

F.evidence: The main problem was that the wheels were set in a single [[7]], which made the skates hard to control.
F.explanation_zh: a single 後面要接名詞，proud 是形容詞。

G.evidence: The main problem was that the wheels were set in a single [[7]], which made the skates hard to control.
G.explanation_zh: a single 後面要接名詞，slow down 是動詞片語。

H.evidence: The main problem was that the wheels were set in a single [[7]], which made the skates hard to control.
H.explanation_zh: a single 後面要接名詞，dangerous 是形容詞。

I.evidence: The main problem was that the wheels were set in a single [[7]], which made the skates hard to control.
I.explanation_zh: a single 後面要接名詞，smashed 是動詞過去式。

J.evidence: He placed four wheels in two pairs, one pair under the toes and one under the heel.
J.explanation_zh: 「輪子裝在單一個重量裡」說不通；後文 four wheels in two pairs 對比的是輪子原本排成一排。

A.evidence: A skater could now turn simply by moving his or her [[8]] to one side, which made skating much safer.
A.explanation_zh: 所有格 his or her 後面要接名詞，popular 是形容詞。

B.evidence: A skater could now turn simply by moving his or her [[8]] to one side, which made skating much safer.
B.explanation_zh: 「把他或她的傷痛移到一邊就能轉彎」說不通；轉彎靠的是移動身體重心。

C.evidence: A skater could now turn simply by moving his or her [[8]] to one side, which made skating much safer.
C.explanation_zh: 「把他或她的客人移到一邊就能轉彎」不合情理；轉彎靠的是移動身體重心。

D.evidence: A skater could now turn simply by moving his or her [[8]] to one side, which made skating much safer.
D.explanation_zh: 所有格 his or her 後面要接名詞，described 是過去分詞。

E.evidence: A skater could now turn simply by moving his or her [[8]] to one side, which made skating much safer.
E.explanation_zh: 「把他或她的一排移到一邊」說不通；兩對輪子的設計讓溜冰者靠重心轉彎。

F.evidence: A skater could now turn simply by moving his or her [[8]] to one side, which made skating much safer.
F.explanation_zh: 所有格 his or her 後面要接名詞，proud 是形容詞。

G.evidence: A skater could now turn simply by moving his or her [[8]] to one side, which made skating much safer.
G.explanation_zh: 所有格 his or her 後面要接名詞，slow down 是動詞片語。

H.evidence: A skater could now turn simply by moving his or her [[8]] to one side, which made skating much safer.
H.explanation_zh: 所有格 his or her 後面要接名詞，dangerous 是形容詞。

I.evidence: A skater could now turn simply by moving his or her [[8]] to one side, which made skating much safer.
I.explanation_zh: 所有格 his or her 後面要接名詞，smashed 是動詞過去式。

B.evidence: As a result, skating soon became [[9]] in America and Europe, where thousands of people bought skates.
B.explanation_zh: hurt 用來形容人受傷，「溜冰變得受傷」說不通；數千人購買溜冰鞋表示溜冰變得流行。

C.evidence: As a result, skating soon became [[9]] in America and Europe, where thousands of people bought skates.
C.explanation_zh: became 後面接單數可數名詞須有冠詞，「溜冰成為客人」也說不通；這裡要形容詞。

D.evidence: As a result, skating soon became [[9]] in America and Europe, where thousands of people bought skates.
D.explanation_zh: skating soon became described 不成語；這裡要形容詞表示溜冰變得流行。

E.evidence: As a result, skating soon became [[9]] in America and Europe, where thousands of people bought skates.
E.explanation_zh: became 後面要形容詞，row 是名詞／動詞，「溜冰成為一排」也說不通。

F.evidence: As a result, skating soon became [[9]] in America and Europe, where thousands of people bought skates.
F.explanation_zh: 活動本身不會自豪；後面說數千人買溜冰鞋，表示的是流行。

G.evidence: As a result, skating soon became [[9]] in America and Europe, where thousands of people bought skates.
G.explanation_zh: became 後面不能接原形動詞片語 slow down。

H.explanation_zh: As a result 承接「讓溜冰安全許多」，結果卻說溜冰變得危險，前後矛盾；後面數千人購買溜冰鞋也表示流行。

I.evidence: As a result, skating soon became [[9]] in America and Europe, where thousands of people bought skates.
I.explanation_zh: skating became smashed「溜冰變得被砸碎」說不通。

J.evidence: As a result, skating soon became [[9]] in America and Europe, where thousands of people bought skates.
